subject: Dedicated capacity renewal — min replicas, warm pool & throughput commitment
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@streamline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Brewer <tom@streamline.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity renewal — request to raise min replicas + warm pool

Hi Karthik,

We're approaching renewal on 2026-12-31 for our Dedicated cluster (current commitment: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs). After analyzing expected batch traffic for Q1, we expect sustained higher tail load during nightly inference windows and three planned monthly batch jobs. To avoid throughput cliffs, we'd like to propose the following changes as part of renewal: 

- Increase committed GPUs by +8 (to 56) dedicated to the production pool.
- Set min_replicas = 4 (current min = 2) for the primary service to ensure baseline throughput.
- Add a warm pool of 2 pre-warmed replicas that can be used for immediate scale-ups (warm pool should maintain KV cache priming).
- Scale-up maximum replicas capped at 12; target p95 latency guarantees for streaming requests during business hours.

Can Redwood provide an updated commercial and an autoscaling policy we can agree to (including scale-up lag tolerances and warm-pool behavior)? We're sensitive to cost, but the business impact of missed SLAs in the batch window is high.

Also attaching our rough traffic chart (attached: nightly-load.csv) to give context.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of ML Infra, Streamline AI
olivia.park@streamline.ai

Attachments:
- nightly-load.csv (csv)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity renewal — request to raise min replicas + warm pool

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detail and the traffic chart. Appreciate the head's up on the monthly batch spikes. 

High level we can accommodate the request, but want to confirm the tradeoffs and lock down autoscale knobs so performance behavior is deterministic:

Option A (Committed uplift, low operational overhead)
- Commit +8 GPUs (56 total); update reserved pool to include 2 GPUs assigned to warm pool.
- min_replicas = 4, warm_pool_size = 2, max_replicas = 12.
- Scale-up action: allocate new replica with KV priming in warm pool first (warm -> active) to reduce cold-starts.
- Commercial: modest uplift to monthly committed fee; we'll provide a 99.5% availability commitment for reserved pool access during your maintenance window.

Option B (Lower commit, faster autoscale)
- Keep committed GPUs at 48, increase warm_pool_size to 3 using burst capacity.
- min_replicas = 3, max_replicas = 14, additional scale-in protections.
- Commercial: fewer committed GPUs but higher burst fees when warm pool or burst is used.

I'm looping in Marissa for the commercial side and Diego for the technical configuration/cost delta. If you can confirm a preference (A or B) and whether you want the warm pool to preserve KV cache across model versions, we'll draft the renewal terms and the autoscale policy template.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Engineer's summary / recommendation:
- Committed GPUs: +8 (56 total) looks reasonable given the nightly sustained throughput. Adds headroom for concurrent batch jobs.
- Autoscale knobs to include in contract (recommended defaults):
  - min_replicas: 4  
  - max_replicas: 12
  - warm_pool_size: 2 (warm instances maintain KV cache and tokenizer priming)
  - warm_pool_retention: 30m (time warm instance stays idle before eviction)
  - scale_up_cooldown: 60s (minimum time between scale-up decisions per group)
  - scale_up_lag_threshold: 1500ms (if queue latency per request > threshold, trigger scale-up path)
  - scale_up_grace_behavior: prefer warm->active conversion for first 2 scale-ups, then allocate new replicas from reserve.

Cost impact (rough, monthly estimate): +8 committed GPUs = ~$32k/month committed delta; warm pool (2 replicas) baked into commit. If you prefer Option B (burst warm pool), expect similar runtime behavior but a higher per-use burst fee (~$0.45/token-equivalent hour).

Operational notes:
- We will instrument per-route token-level telemetry and add a rollback throttling policy so scale decisions can be temporarily limited during noisy spikes.
- For KV cache persistence across model switchover, we recommend explicit cache migration windows; preserving across minor model patching is supported, across major architecture changes is not guaranteed.

Let me know if you'd like me to draft the technical appendix to attach to the commercial terms.

— Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Key commercial terms (high level):
- Committed capacity: 56 GPUs (8 GPU uplift) for 12 months.
- Monthly committed fee: see PDF (summary lines included).
- Autoscale appendix (attached) will be appended to the Master Services Agreement and includes the following enforceable parameters:
  - min_replicas = 4
  - max_replicas = 12
  - warm_pool_size = 2 (maintain KV cache priming)
  - warm_pool_retention = 30m
  - scale_up_cooldown = 60s
  - scale_up_lag_threshold = 1500ms
  - SLA: reserved pool access 99.5% during agreed maintenance window; throughput guarantee: baseline provisioning to sustain 1200 qps across production routes (see appendix for route mapping)

Next steps:
1) If terms look good, sign the amendment (DocuSign link in the PDF and below).

3) Diego will open a runbook for failure modes and add a short-circuit fallback policy to your routes.
